overview: After 1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 Black strikes in the centre with 2...d5. Play usually follows 3.exd5 Nf6 or 3.Bxd5 Nf6 4.Bb3 Nxe4, where Black regains the pawn at once and gets a comfortable game. The result is an open, roughly equal position.

white_ideas.idea: Take on d5 and hold the extra pawn if Black does not recover it
Develop with Nf3 and castle, using the bishop on c4 or b3

black_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn with ...Nf6 and ...Nxd5 or ...Nxe4
Develop actively and hit the centre

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file after the e-pawns trade
Near-symmetrical central structure once the pawn is recovered

character.notes: A direct central break that equalises with simple moves.

gambit.notes: Black normally regains the pawn by force, so it is a gambit in name only.

soundness.notes: Black is theoretically fine; the central break is a recognised equaliser.

structure.notes: Open: the e- and d-pawns come off early.

approach.notes: A sideline of the Bishop's Opening, but a standard Black reply.

level.notes: A direct line with a clear idea.

sublines_that_differ.name: Bxd5 line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 d5 3. Bxd5 Nf6 4. Bb3 Nxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black regains the pawn at once; White keeps only the bishop on b3.

character.reason: Open equal play, neither especially forcing nor especially safe.

gambit.reason: The pawn comes back by force, so no real gambit.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and pieces get open lines.

approach.reason: Rare line but a normal choice at all levels.

level.reason: A direct central idea, not a long theory line.
